Article Title: PM Modi calls Sharad Pawar; advises complete rest
Article Text:
The 85-year-old veteran politician was admitted to a private hospital in Pune on Monday, then discharges 2 days later

We along with Supriya will look after the country, you focus on recovery, PM tells Pawar

PUNE: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday called NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar to enquire about his health after the veteran politician was discharged from a private hospital in Pune."Prime Minister Modi called up Pawar Saheb this morning to enquire about his health. He spoke with great warmth and respect and suggested that Pawar Saheb take complete rest," Vitthal Maniyar, a close associate of Sharad Pawar, told the media in Pune on Wednesday.Maniyar said PM Modi urged Pawar not to worry about work and to focus on his recovery."The PM told Pawar Saheb that Supriya is now ready and that he, along with Supriya, will look after the country, while Pawar should focus on his health," Maniyar said.Pawar thanked the Prime Minister for enquiring about his health and assured him that he would take rest.The 85-year-old veteran politician was admitted to a private hospital in Pune on Monday morning after complaining of pleuritic pain. After undergoing treatment for two days, he was discharged on Wednesday.In an official statement, Dr Purvez K Grant, chairman and managing trustee of Ruby Hall Clinic, said, "Sharad Pawar has been discharged from the hospital today. He is stable and doing well. He will be travelling directly from the hospital to his residence in Mumbai."
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi called NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar to enquire about his health. The 85-year-old veteran politician was admitted to a private hospital in Pune on Monday, then discharges 2 days later. PM Modi urged Pawar not to worry about work and to focus on recovery.

Article Title: Judge facing rape charge presides over Pocso court
Article Text:
SC seeks Allahabad HC's response to a rape complainant's plea to suspend a UP judge who has been chargesheeted for rape and heads a POCSO court.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Can a UP additional district judge, chargesheeted for rape by Delhi police for allegedly sexually exploiting a woman, head a Pocso court which decides criminal cases against persons accused of sexually assaulting minors? Supreme Court has agreed to examine this petition filed by the rape complainant.A bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice Monday on the petition and sought response from Allahabad high court on her plea for suspension of the senior judicial officer.Appearing for the petitioner, advocate Rakesh Kumar Singh told the bench that at least judicial work should be withdrawn from the judge, but the Allahabad HC had rejected her petition.The bench in a cryptic order said, "Issue notice, returnable on Dec 11."The petitioner had lodged an FIR at Mayur Vihar police station on Dec 8, 2022 accusing the judicial officer, whom she met on a matrimonial site, of making repeated false promises to marry to establish a physical relationship with her.Delhi Police in Jan 2023 sought permission from Allahabad HC to proceed against the judicial officer. Two months later, Delhi HC granted the judge interim protection from arrest but allowed police to continue the investigations, she said.Police later recorded her statement before a magistrate.Police in June 2023 sent a reminder to Allahabad HC for early decision on request to proceed in investigations against the judicial officer but were informed by the HC that a vigilance inquiry was already going on against him. In Oct 2024, the chief justice of Allahabad HC permitted investigations, and the HC directed the judicial officer to cooperate with the probe.In April 2025, Delhi police informed the Allahabad HC regarding proposal to file chargesheet against the judge and on May 5 last year, the chargesheet was filed against the additional district judge under Section 376 IPC (rape). In Nov last year, Delhi HC allowed the trial court to proceed with the chargesheet but continued the interim order protecting the judicial officer from arrest.On May 23, the chief metropolitan magistrate of Karkardooma courts in Delhi took cognisance of the chargesheet, leading the complainant to file a petition before Allahabad HC seeking suspension of the officer. She moved SC after HC declined her plea.
Article Summary: SC seeks Allahabad HC's response to a rape complainant's plea to suspend a UP judge who has been chargesheeted for rape and heads a POCSO court. The bench in a cryptic order said, "Issue notice, returnable on Dec 11."

NEW DELHI: Congress on Tuesday launched a sharp attack on Union home minister Amit Shah over the formation of a new political outfit, the Arunachal Janata Party.In a post on X, Congress leader Jairam Ramesh shared a "public notice" and alleged that the new party had been formed in a manner similar to the revival of the Nationalist Citizens Party of India by Shah as a "parking place" for TMC defectors."Undoubtedly, a move by the self-styled Chanakya who revived an unknown Nationalist Citizens Party of India as a parking place for TMC defectors," Jairam Ramesh said."There are 734 such registered unrecognised political parties in India that had a reported income of over Rs 1,100 crore in 2024-25. Article Text:
Though the bench initially asked Khan why he did not move the Allahabad HC, it agreed to list the matter for hearing.

NEW DELHI: SP leader and ten time MLA Azam Khan on Monday moved Supreme Court challenging the ED decision to arrest him on stepping out of Rampur jail after Allahabad HC granted him bail in the last of the 95 cases, which have been slapped on him after BJP came to power in Uttar Pradesh in 2017.Advocate Mohd Nizamuddin Pasha told a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the arrest by ED in a 2019 case, in which FIR itself was registered 13 years after the allegations about land purchase transactions fo Jauhar University from farmers, was illegal.Though the bench initially asked Khan why he did not move the Allahabad HC, it agreed to list the matter for hearing. Khan said he was forced to move the SC because of “blatant illegality of his arrest including the manner and timing and the gross abuse of process and mala fide exercise of power whereby the machinery of criminal justice system is used for political ends to keep an opposition leader indefinitely in incarceration particularly on account of the approaching assembly elections in UP. ”Seeking invocation of SC’s exclusive Article 142 powers for grant of interim bail, Khan said since 2017, he has been made an accused in 95 criminal cases, including the ED case. He has been acquitted in six cases, and three cases were closed after his complicity could not be proved.“He has been convicted in six; in four of these his sentence has been suspended and/or his conviction stayed, and in the other two, the sentence of two years has been undergone.The remaining 80 cases are pending trial. The clear pattern that emerges is that whenever the Petitioner is about to be released, a fresh case is registered or revived, and he is sought to be kept behind bars,” Khan alleged.The 78-year-old petitioner, who had also been a UP cabinet minister as member of both Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha, complained that he was illegally arrested in a 7-year-old ECIR from the gate of District Jail Rampur on Oct 31 without providing him with the arrest memo or written grounds and reasons for arrest.Khan said, while being lodged in Rampur Jail, ED had questioned him relating to the case and recorded his statements under PMLA and hence there was no basis for the ED to arrest him against and seek judicial custody. “Timing of my arrest is wholly mala fide and politically motivated,” the SP leader said, claiming that he suffered from serious kidney, urinary and other age-related ailments. And that he has spent more than 5 years in prison since Feb 2020.
Article Summary: Azam Khan on Monday moved Supreme Court challenging the ED decision to arrest him on stepping out of Rampur jail after Allahabad HC granted him bail. Khan said he was forced to move the SC because of ‘blatant illegality of his arrest’

Article Title: Rouse Avenue court seeks Delhi Police response on Bimol Akoijam's anticipatory bail plea
Article Text:
Former JNU professor and Congress MP Bimol Akoijam (PTI file photo)

NEW DELHI: The Rouse Avenue Court on Tuesday issued notice to Delhi Police on the anticipatory bail plea of Manipur MP and former Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) professor Bimol Akoijam in a sexual harassment case and extended his interim protection till November 5.Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh sought the police response and directed the investigating agency to place on record the complaint filed by JNU students against Akoijam. The matter has been listed for arguments on November 5.Akoijam is seeking anticipatory bail in an FIR registered at Vasant Kunj North police station following allegations of sexual harassment levelled by 11 JNU students against him when he was working as a professor at the university.Additional Public Prosecutor Manish Rawat appeared for Delhi Police and accepted the notice. The police have already filed a reply before the Patiala House Court.During the hearing, Akoijam's counsel submitted that the complaint was made by a group of students to the dean and not by any aggrieved woman directly. The counsel also said the university's Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) had examined the matter and its report had been annexed to the bail application.The defence further submitted that Akoijam had cooperated with the investigation and appeared before the investigating officer, while the alleged complainant was not joining the probe. The counsel also pointed out that the high court had stayed his termination from the university.Akoijam had initially secured transit anticipatory bail from a Manipur court on October 12, which was extended till October 20 and subsequently till October 29.He then approached the Patiala House Court, which granted him interim protection till November 2. However, the court held that it could not hear his anticipatory bail plea as he is a sitting MP, and that the matter fell within the jurisdiction of the Rouse Avenue Court.The investigating officer had also opposed the plea on the jurisdictional ground. Following the transfer of the case, Akoijam moved the Rouse Avenue Court for anticipatory bail.
Article Summary: Akoijam is seeking anticipatory bail in an FIR registered at Vasant Kunj North police station. He is accused of sexual harassment levelled by 11 JNU students against him. The matter has been listed for arguments on November 5.

Article Title: 'Rs 25cr spent on ads to claim no stubble burning, FIRs tell another story': BJP targets AAP govt in Punjab
Article Text:
Rs 20-25 crore was spent on advertisements to project that there was no stubble burning in the state, said

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Delhi Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa on Tuesday accused the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government in Punjab of allowing and facilitating stubble burning while spending Rs 20-25 crore on advertisements claiming that no farm fires were taking place in the state. He alleged that the government was then registering FIRs against farmers for stubble burning, even as it publicly denied the practice.He also questioned the appointment of former AAP spokesperson Reena Gupta as chairperson of the Punjab Pollution Control Board, alleging that the move was aimed at manipulating pollution data.Addressing a press conference in Delhi, Sirsa claimed that Punjab had recorded more than 1,000 incidents of stubble burning and alleged that the state government was trying to conceal the extent of the problem through publicity campaigns.“Advertisements worth Rs 20-25 crore were released to claim that stubble burning was not taking place in Punjab this year. On the other hand, I am handing over copies of all the FIRs, district-wise, to you. These are all FIRs registered in connection with stubble burning,” he said, displaying documents that he claimed contained details of the cases, further alleging that "Punjab Police and Punjab government officers are facilitating the burning of stubble.Taking aim at AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal, Sirsa alleged that the party had brought its political spokesperson from Delhi to head the Punjab Pollution Control Board to influence the reporting of pollution data.“For the first time in Punjab's history, a non-Punjabi, non-IAS, non-technical person has been appointed to such a position. They have appointed their political spokesperson, who is said to be a close relative of Arvind Kejriwal, as the chairperson of the Punjab Pollution Control Board after bringing her from Delhi,” Sirsa said.He identified the appointee as Reena Gupta, alleging that she was being projected as the face of the campaign to deny the scale of stubble burning in Punjab. Sirsa claimed the appointment was intended to “conceal the truth by fudging data”.Sirsa sought to contrast Punjab's situation with Delhi's air quality, claiming that the national capital had recorded 220 clean-air days in 2026, the highest in a decade. He also said October was the cleanest in the past 10 years and that the average air quality index (AQI) had improved by 10 per cent compared with previous years.Appealing to Kejriwal and AAP leader Manish Sisodia not to undermine Delhi's efforts to improve air quality, Sirsa said, “By setting fires in Punjab, you are once again causing the situation in Delhi to deteriorate.”
Article Summary: Manjinder Singh Sirsa accuses Punjab government of allowing and facilitating stubble burning while spending Rs 20-25 crore on advertisements. He also questioned the appointment of former AAP spokesperson Reena Gupta as chairperson of the Punjab Pollution Control Board. Sirsa claimed the appointment was intended to “conceal the truth by fudging data”

Article Title: 'Doesn’t have courage to call all-party meet?’: Congress questions Shah over delay in discussion on delimitation Bill

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Tuesday questioned the Centre over the delay in proroguing Parliament, alleging that the government was considering convening a special session to push delimitation-related bills. He also challenged the Centre to share its proposals with the opposition and convene an all-party meeting to discuss them.In a post on X, Ramesh said 82 days had passed since the Monsoon Session of Parliament was adjourned sine die, but it had still not been prorogued. He alleged that Union home minister Amit Shah was continuing to explore the possibility of calling a special session to pass the delimitation bills."The content of these Bills is still not known although its intent is clear—to save the BJP from the debacle that is staring it in 2029," Ramesh alleged.Taking a swipe at Shah, the Congress leader also referred to his remarks about holding a special session to discuss allegations of vote theft. Ramesh questioned the apparent difference in the government's approach, recalling that Shah had earlier declined the opposition's demand for a debate on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, saying it was the Election Commission's prerogative."Meanwhile, the self-styled Chanakya, the master of bluff, bombast and bluster says he is ready for a Special Session to discuss vote chori.Last year, when the combined Opposition wanted a debate on SIR he had refused saying SIR was the prerogative of the Election Commission.If the Home Minister is serious about a Special Session on vote chori, he should first secure the resignation of his hatchet man CEC Gyanesh Kumar. He should also suspend SIR," Ramesh said.He further demanded that the government share its proposed delimitation changes with the Opposition well in advance and asked why Shah was not convening an all-party meeting to discuss the proposals in detail."Why doesn't he have the courage to convene an All-Party meeting to discuss these proposals in detail?" Ramesh asked.
Article Summary: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh questioned the Centre over the delay in proroguing Parliament. He alleged that the government was considering convening a special session to push delimitation-related bills. He also challenged the Centre to share its proposals with the opposition and convene an all-party meeting to discuss them.

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke in another X post on Monday claimed that the local Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in his hometown had “suddenly gone on leave” and that a new officer had been brought in to take charge.Dipke’s remarks came amid party's earlier claim that he and fellow CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Dass could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other provisions.AISA national president Neha Bora on Monday claimed that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station.In a post on X, Neha said "Rosy and other protesting journalists are detained at Delhi Cantt PS. Article Title: Shiv Sena corporator Meenakshi Shinde seeks police protection for slain UBT functionary’s family, alleges conspiracy to frame her and Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde
Article Text:
File pic of former Thane Municipal Corporation mayor and Shiv Sena leader Meenakshi Shinde arriving at the Anti-Extortion Cell for questioning in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Pradeep Purnekar in Thane

Thane:





Former Thane mayor and Shiv Sena corporator Meenakshi Shinde on Tuesday approached Thane police commissioner Ashutosh Dumbare seeking additional police protection for the family of slain Shiv Sena (UBT) Manpada division chief Pradeep Purnekar and three local residents, citing an alleged conspiracy by the Opposition to implicate her and deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde in the case.The move comes even as the Purnekar family has named Meenakshi as the alleged mastermind behind the murder.Meenakshi claimed she had received inputs about a series of meetings being held to implicate her and the deputy CM. “I was alerted by one of them (Opposition) about regular meetings being held to falsely implicate me and (Eknath) Shinde in some way or the other, for which they may go to any extent. A fake audio clip naming three locals was also circulated during the 2026 civic elections. We fear for their lives too and have sought additional protection for them,” she told reporters.Defending her resignation as Thane district chief of Shiv Sena’s women’s wing, Meenakshi said it was voluntary and driven by her inability to watch Eknath Shinde being repeatedly targeted.Dismissing suggestions of a personal rivalry with the Purnekars, Meenakshi said she was not even contesting against them in the same electoral panel. Instead, she pointed to alleged differences between the family and former MP Rajan Vichare, claiming he had not campaigned for Pradeep’s wife Vijeta and his brother Jaynath, who contested the civic elections.Meanwhile, the Purnekars are learnt to be considering approaching Bombay High Court after their meeting with chief minister Devendra Fadnavis on Sunday, expressing dissatisfaction over the pace of the Thane police probe.
Article Summary: Former Thane mayor and Shiv Sena corporator Meenakshi Shinde on Tuesday approached Thane police commissioner Ashutosh Dumbare seeking additional police protection for the family of Pradeep Purnekar and three local residents. She claimed she had received inputs about a series of meetings being held to implicate her and the deputy CM.

Article Title: Shiv Sena (UBT)’s Pradeep Purnekar murder: DCP heading SIT retains posting; Thane police to reconstruct timeline in alleged custodial torture of two men
Article Text:
Pradeep Purnekar

Thane:





Deputy commissioner of police (DCP) of Thane Crime Branch Amarsinh Jadhav, who heads the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing Shiv Sena (UBT) Manpada division chief Pradeep Purnekar’s Sept murder along with DCP Prashant Kadam, will continue in his present posting.Kadam is also overseeing the inquiry into the alleged custodial assault of two men who were arrested by Kapurbawdi police station for rioting in Manpada on Oct 29.The two 26-year-olds — one from Manpada and the other from Manorama Nagar — had alleged that a police sub-inspector and a police naik had subjected them to torture inside the station premises. “We are scrutinising the CCTV footage of the police station and will record statements of all personnel present on duty. The two staffers named by the youths have already been transferred to the control room to ensure zero interference in the probe. We will not spare anyone found guilty,” Kadam confirmed.Police said the two men have undergone medical examination and samples have been sent to the forensic laboratory. The reports are expected to establish whether there was any contact with a foreign object in their private parts, as alleged.Police are yet to record detailed statements from the two complainants, despite repeated requests. It is hinted the men may be currently away from the city.
Article Summary: DCP Amarsinh Jadhav heads the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing Shiv Sena (UBT) Manpada division chief Pradeep Purnekar’s Sept murder along with DCP Prashant Kadam. Kadam is also overseeing the inquiry into the alleged custodial assault of two men who were arrested by Kapurbawdi police station.

Article Title: Inebriated man held for pelting stones at police commissionerate
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





A 50-year-old intoxicated man was arrested on Monday night for allegedly entering the police commissionerate premises in the Mill Corner area and pelting stones at the building, shattering its glass door and causing damage worth around Rs 50,000 to govt property.“The accused, identified as Chandrakant Vitthal Magre of Pethenagar in Bhausinghpura, was arrested soon after the incident,” said Begumpura police inspector Pravina Yadav.He was produced before the court on Tuesday and was remanded in one-day police custody.According to the complaint lodged by police head constable Nagnath Bhanudas Kendre, the accused allegedly threw stones at the commissionerate building without any apparent reason. “The impact shattered the glass panel of the entrance, resulting in damage to govt property,” the complaint said.Following the incident, the police guards present on duty rushed to the spot and nabbed him and found him to be inebriated. Sub-inspector Tupe is conducting further investigation to ascertain the circumstances that led to the incident.
Article Summary: A 50-year-old intoxicated man was arrested on Monday night for allegedly entering the police commissionerate premises and pelting stones at the building. Chandrakant Vitthal Magre of Pethenagar in Bhausinghpura, was arrested soon after the incident. He was produced before the court on Tuesday and was remanded in one-day police custody.

Article Title: Gang robs 3 of gold jewellery on Mahalaxmi Express near Satara
Article Text:
Kolhapur:





A gang of thieves allegedly robbed three women passengers of gold jewellery worth around Rs 2 lakh after stopping Mumbai-Kolhapur Mahalaxmi Express by tampering with the railway signal system near Salpa station in Satara district around 2.30am on Sunday.Taking advantage of the halt, five to six gang members allegedly entered reserved coach S2 and targeted sleeping women passengers. They snatched their gold jewellery and fled.Separate cases have been registered with Lonand RPF for signal vandalism and Miraj railway police for the jewellery theft. Police are investigating the incident with the help of a dog squad and a forensic team.Sunita Gorakshnath Tupe (40), a Kanjurmarg East resident, lodged a complaint at Miraj Govt Railway Police (GRP) station. The stolen jewellery also belonged to fellow passenger Surekha Babasaheb Khade (40), a resident of Khopoli in Raigad district. The women were travelling to Kolhapur to attend a family function.Inspector Sitaram Phand of Miraj railway police, said, “The gang comprised around eight to ten members, with five to six of them allegedly entering the coaches. Some members are suspected to have remained near the signal system while others targeted passengers inside the train.”After the thieves jumped off the train, some passengers tried to chase them. However, the gang allegedly pelted stones at coaches S2, S3 and S5 while escaping, triggering panic.“The manner in which the train was stopped, followed by the robbery and stone-pelting, has raised suspicions that the incident was pre-planned. The exact manner in which the signal system was tampered with will be a key part of the investigation. We have formed several teams and a search operation is under way to trace them,” added Phand.
Article Summary: Gang of thieves allegedly robbed three women passengers of gold jewellery worth around Rs 2 lakh. They stopped Mumbai-Kolhapur Mahalaxmi Express by tampering with the railway signal system near Salpa station in Satara district around 2.30am on Sunday. Police are investigating the incident with the help of a dog squad and a forensic team.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: 2 women escape from RPF lockup in Navi Mumbai; 1 held after 6 hours, cop suspended
Article Text:
The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. (AI image)





NAVI MUMBAI: In a major security lapse at Belapur Railway Protection Force (RPF), two women arrested for allegedly attempting to steal overhead electric wires from the Juinagar railway godown escaped from the lockup after midnight on September 28.One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large.The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated against her.As per the FIR registered by RPF sub-inspector Milap Parte (52) at Panvel GRP, a case was registered on September 24 under Section 3(a) of the Railway Property (Unauthorized Possession) Act, 1966, Amendment 2012, at Belapur railway police station.The case was based on a written memo submitted by RPF personnel Ravikant Gade regarding the theft of overhead electric wires from the godown at Juinagar railway station on September 21.During the probe, a trap was laid on September 26 and around 1pm, two women were found loitering suspiciously near the Juinagar godown with the alleged intention of committing theft.They were taken into custody and identified as Rupali Kailas Kurhade (30), from Jalna, and Shalibai Ashok Pawar (49), from Bhiwandi.They were arrested after an FIR was registered for attempted theft and produced before a CSMT court, which remanded them to police custody till September 30. They were lodged in the lockup at Belapur RPF police station.Day-shift woman constable Rakhi Malaiya was assigned guard duty at the lockup, after which woman head constable Pooja Bagre was on night duty.Around 2am on September 28, when Bagre had gone to the toilet, the two women allegedly managed to open the lock by inserting their hands through the iron bars of the lockup and jerking it. Police suspect the lock may not have been secured properly.The women then reached the balcony at the rear end of the police station. They removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping.The incident was captured on CCTV footage. PSI Parte learnt about the escape after waking up at home around 6.30am and finding several missed calls from head constable Bagre and ASI Rajiv Parsan.Sunil Nila, chief spokesperson of Central Railway, said, "One accused woman Rupali Kurhade was apprehended from near Nerul railway station around 8.45 am. The other accused Shalibai Pawar is still absconding."
Article Summary: The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large. The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated.

Article Title: TMC suspends fire chief over immersion ghats lapses
Article Text:
Thane municipal corporation





THANE: The Thane municipal corporation (TMC) on Friday suspended its acting chief fire officer (CFO) over alleged negligence in providing adequate safety equipment at idol immersion ghats on Oct 20. Article Title: Ahmednagar district central cooperative bank election results today, regional leaders vie for control
Article Text:
Former MP Sujay Vikhe casts his vote during the election on Monday

Nashik:

FIR for shooting video of voting process





Voting for 10 seats of Ahmednagar District Central Cooperative Bank was conducted on Monday across 33 polling centres in Ahilyanagar district amid high political intensity as prominent regional leaders fight for control over the vital agrarian financial institution.Out of 21 seats of directors on the board, 11 were secured uncontested prior to the polls. The ruling cooperative panel, led by district guardian minister Radhakrishna Vikhe and former minister Balasaheb Thorat, secured 10 of these uncontested seats. The faction headed by Legislative Council Speaker Ram Shinde bagged one seat. This early edge gave the Vikhe-Thorat alliance a decisive majority even before the polling for the remaining segments.“A total of 27 candidates are in the fray for the 10 contested slots. A total of 3,809 voters out of 3,837 cast their votes on Monday. Results will be declared on Tuesday,” said returning officer Mangesh Suravse, also the district deputy registrar of Ahilyanagar.High-profile electoral battles were seen in constituencies such as Akole, Karjat and Parner, where supporters of Lok Sabha MP Nilesh Lanke and former MP Sadashiv Lokhande fielded candidates against the Vikhe-Thorat panel.In Karjat, the Vikhe-Thorat panel is pitted against the Ram Shinde-led panel in a direct contest.After casting his vote, NCP (SP) MP Lanke said, “It is a battle between the established and the deprived, and we have the habit of taking on the established ones and defeating them.” He said contesting was vital to ensure the survival of the bank.Former MP Sujay Vikhe said voters support cooperation over party-level politics, prompting leaders Radhakrishna Vikhe, Balasaheb Thorat and NCP MLA Sangram Jagtap to form a consensus panel. “The voters have always refused party-level politics and instead supported people on the basis of their work. Since people here support cooperation, you can see we joined hands to have a panel to evolve a consensus, and we believe we have been successful,” said Sujay Vikhe.Returning officer Suravse ordered that a police complaint be lodged over a breach of voting secrecy at centre number 27 in Bhikaji Tukaram Meher Secondary School in Sangamner, as a video circulated on social media showing a voter revealing his ballot paper inside the booth. Another person allegedly recorded his act on a cellphone.Suravse directed regional officer Santosh Kore and centre head Dilip Chature to submit an incident report and file an FIR against both individuals at the local police station for violating the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Election Rules 2014 and sections of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
Article Summary: Out of 21 seats of directors on the board, 11 were secured uncontested prior to the polls. The ruling cooperative panel, led by district guardian minister Radhakrishna Vikhe and former minister Balasaheb Thorat, secured 10 of these uncontested seats. The faction headed by Legislative Council Speaker Ram Shinde bagged one seat.

Article Title: Robbers loot Rs 3 crore from courier vehicle on Mumbai-Agra highway in Dhule
Article Text:
Nashik:





A gang of five to six robbers intercepted a courier SUV on Mumbai-Agra highway near Palasner village in Dhule and fled with Rs 3.06 crore between 12.30am and 12.45am on Saturday. SUV driver told police that the robbers smashed the window with iron rods, dragged him out, assaulted and blindfolded him before forcing him and his colleague into their vehicle.The Shirpur Taluka police have registered an FIR under relevant sections of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for robbery, assault and wrongful confinement. Inspector Jaypal Hire said, “Three teams have been formed to ascertain the identity of the criminals involved in the robbery and trace them.”“Owing to the Diwali holidays, employees at the firm’s Bhopal branch had been directed to transfer cash collections to its Mumbai office,” police said.Acting on the instructions, two employees left Bhopal around 6pm on Friday in an SUV carrying the cash. After entering Maharashtra around 12.15am, their SUV was intercepted by a multipurpose vehicle (MPV) near Palasner.In his complaint, the SUV driver said five to six men got out of the MPV, smashed the driver’s-side window using iron pipes and rods, dragged him out and assaulted him.The attackers allegedly blindfolded him and forced him into their vehicle before driving away.The complainant told police that the MPV halted briefly at a location before moving again. “Later, both he and his colleague, who had also been blindfolded, were pushed out of the vehicle. The assailants handed over the keys to their SUV, but the vehicle was not nearby,” police said, citing the complaint.The duo walked to a nearby village, contacted firm officials using a villager’s cellphone and began searching for the SUV. “They eventually located the vehicle, but a bag containing Rs 3.06 crore was missing,” police said.Police said investigations were under way and suspected the accused might have fled back to neighbouring Madhya Pradesh. “Three teams have been formed to ascertain the identity of the criminals involved in the robbery and trace them,” inspector Hire said.
Article Summary: A gang of five to six robbers intercepted a courier SUV on Mumbai-Agra highway near Palasner village in Dhule. SUV driver told police that the robbers smashed the window with iron rods, dragged him out, assaulted and blindfolded him before forcing him and his colleague into their vehicle.

Article Title: ‘A remedy that depends on CM’s personal intervention is no remedy at all’: Madras high court on professor’s wrongful detention
Article Text:
Madras high court responded to the wrongful detention case involving CM Joseph Vijay and A Kalaiyarasan (File photo)





CHENNAI: Four days after chief minister C Joseph Vijay met Madras institute of development studies (MIDS) associate professor A Kalaiyarasan and regretted his wrongful detention over a fake social media post, Madras high court said, “an apology, however high its source, is not accountability”.“And a remedy that depends on the CM’s personal intervention is not a remedy at all,” Justice N Ramesh said. “...that gentleman’s eminence secured his release within hours and an audience at Secretariat; a common citizen with no access to power, taken at dawn on the same mistaken complaint, would have tasted the lock-up, the remand and the long road of a trial before anyone asked whether the account was even his,” the judge added.The measure of a police force is not how it treats the eminent when press is watching, but how it treats the unknown when nobody is.It is against that measure that handling of political speech—this case included—falls to be judged, the court said.The court made the observations while granting anticipatory bail to DMK councillor D Sudha, who apprehended arrest in connection with a criminal case registered against her for alleged derogatory remarks against the CM.“A govt confident of itself meets criticism with argument, mockery with performance, and abuse — where it truly crosses the line — with remedy, the law of defamation provides. Magnanimity towards political speech is not a grace the state may extend or withhold; it is what the Constitution exacts of those who hold power over their critics,” the court said.As to the alleged derogatory speech made by the councillor, the court said, “This state has a platform tradition older than the republic, whose great practitioners proved that Tamil oratory can wound without descending to filth; an elected representative owes the discourse at least that much. Her own party seniors told her as much at the venue, and to her credit she accepted it — publicly, and on oath, before any court asked her to. ”
Article Summary: Madras high court responded to the wrongful detention case involving CM Joseph Vijay and A Kalaiyarasan. The court made the observations while granting anticipatory bail to DMK councillor D Sudha, who apprehended arrest in connection with a criminal case registered against her for alleged derogatory remarks.

Train's front windshield shattered

Chennai:

Article Title: Former AIADMK MLA, others booked for insulting and intimidating petrol bunk employees near Dharmapuri
Article Text: DHARMAPURI: A case has been registered under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act against A Govindasamy, former Pappireddipatti AIADMK MLA, and others on charges of humiliating and intimidating petrol bunk employees near Dharmapuri.The complainant is R Arunkumar, 37, of Vellalapatti, who has been working at CKM Bharat Petrol Bunk in Rajapettai for the past six months. In his complaint, Arunkumar stated that Govindasamy and his accomplices, numbering more than 30, arrived at the petrol bunk around 10.45am on Oct 26.Arunkumar alleged that the former MLA obstructed vehicles entering the bunk for refuelling and verbally abused him using obscene language and caste-based slurs. Arunkumar stated that his coworker, Nandakumar, who questioned the behaviour, was also assaulted by those who accompanied the former MLA.Arunkumar approached the Dharmapuri superintendent of police A K Arun Kabilan on Friday seeking action against Govindasamy and others under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.Following an inquiry led by Dharmapuri deputy superintendent of Police Sivaraman, a case was registered against the former MLA and others at the Dharmapuri Town B-1 police station.

Article Title: Madapuram temple guard custodial death: Madras HC dismisses pleas of 4 cops, sets 9-month trial deadline
Article Text:
Madras HC





MADURAI: The Madras high court on Wednesday directed the trial court to complete the trial within nine months in the case relating to the custodial death of Madapuram temple security guard B Ajith Kumar in Thiruppuvanam, Sivaganga district, in 2025.Justice P Murugan dismissed petitions filed by four police personnel — then Manamadurai DSP Shanmugasundaram, then Thiruppuvanam inspector of police Ramesh Kumar, then sub-inspector Sivakumar and then head constable Ilayaraja — challenging the court's order remanding them to judicial custody.According to the prosecution, Ajith Kumar, who worked as a security guard at the Batharakaliamman temple in Madapuram, died during custodial interrogation on June 28, 2025. Police had picked him up for questioning in connection with an alleged theft of gold jewellery from a car owned by Nikitha of Madurai district. She and her mother had visited the temple the previous day.The state government transferred the custodial death case and the connected jewellery theft case to the CBI, which arrested six police personnel — Prabhu, Kannan, Sankaramanikandan, Raja, Ananth and Ramachandran, the driver of the van in which Ajith Kumar was transported.Initially, the CBI filed its final report before the fifth additional district and sessions court in Madurai against six police personnel. Subsequently, it filed a supplementary chargesheet naming four more police personnel — then Manamadurai DSP Shanmugasundaram, then Thiruppuvanam inspector of police Ramesh Kumar, then sub-inspector Sivakumar and then head constable Ilayaraja — as accused in the case, in addition to the six personnel already arrested.
Article Summary: B Ajith Kumar died during custodial interrogation on June 28, 2025. Police had picked him up for questioning in connection with an alleged theft of gold jewellery from a car owned by Nikitha of Madurai district. The state government transferred the custodial death case and the connected jewellery theft case to the CBI.

Article Title: Activist Mugilan arrested for non-appearance In jallikattu case hearings
Article Text:
Madurai

:





Cleared/270 WordsMadurai district CB-CID Madurai police have arrested environmental activist R S Mugilan at Erode on Monday night for not appearing before the court for a hearing in a jallikattu case registered against him. Later, he was granted bail on health grounds.According to sources, Mugilan hasn't appeared for hearings for the past three months, citing medical reasons. Subsequently, a non-bailable warrant was issued against him. He was arrested at Erode.He was produced before a judicial magistrate in Madurai; after Mugilan cited health reasons for non-appearance for hearing, he was released on bail by the magistrate.Speaking to reporters after appearing before the court, Mugilan alleged that he was illegally detained despite informing the authorities about his medical condition.“A case registered against four of us in connection with the jallikattu protest held in Madurai in 2017 is currently under trial. I have been undergoing medical treatment for the past three months due to health issues and was therefore unable to appear before the court. I had informed the CB-CID police about my health condition and told them that I would appear before the court during the next hearing and seek cancellation of the warrant.However, while I was travelling on a road in Perundurai in Erode district, police intercepted and arrested me,” the activist said.He claimed that police did not allow him to inform anyone about his arrest. “Though I was detained around 9pm on Monday, the arrest memo was provided only on Tuesday morning. I was also denied permission to speak with my lawyers and was allowed to inform them only after a protest,” Mugilan said.
Article Summary: Environmental activist R S Mugilan was arrested at Erode on Monday night. Mugilan hasn't appeared for hearings for the past three months, citing medical reasons. A non-bailable warrant was issued against him. Later, he was granted bail on health grounds.

Article Title: 3 officials held in graft cases
Article Text: Madurai: Tenkasi district DVAC officials arrested the village administrative officer (VAO) of Vengadampatti, Chermapandian, on Tuesday on charges of demanding and accepting a bribe of Rs 4,000 from Thamotharan for taking action on his petition seeking patta. Similarly, Theni DVAC officials arrested a VAO for accepting a bribe of Rs 20,000 for taking action on a petition seeking patta. In a separate incident on Monday, Virudhunagar district DVAC officials arrested Tangedco assistant engineer of Veeracholan village, Ramamoorthy, for accepting a bribe of Rs 2,000 from Pichaimuthu for taking action on his petition seeking an increase in the electricity load.

Article Title: Murder suspect arrested near Krishnagiri
Article Text: KRISHNAGIRI: The Krishnagiri district police on Saturday arrested a man on charges of murdering a 70- year-old woman in Pannandur village.District superintendent of police GS Anitha said, Chamundeeswari, who was living alone, was found dead under suspicious circumstances in her house on Friday morning.During investigations, police found that Suryakumar alias Surya,30, of the same village entered Chamundeeswari’s house around 1am on Friday with an intention to steal valuables. “Acting on the findings, special police teams launched a search operation and arrested the man within 12 hours of the crime,” the SP said.
Article Summary: Chamundeeswari, who was living alone, was found dead under suspicious circumstances in her house on Friday morning. Police found that Suryakumar alias Surya,30, of the same village entered the house with an intention to steal valuables.

Article Title: PE teacher suspended after national flag turns upside down at state sports meet in Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A physical education teacher has been suspended following a protocol lapse during the opening ceremony of the state-level 67th Republic Day Athletics Competitions held at the Mahatma Gandhi Sports Ground here on Wednesday.The incident occurred when the state transport minister A Vijay Tamilan Parthiban was hoisting the national flag, and a snag in the rope caused the flag to fly upside down. The event was organized by the state school education department.Taking immediate note of the negligence during the flag-hoisting ceremony, Salem chief educational officer A Ellappan issued an order placing physical education teacher John Jamindar who had supervised the flag hoisting area.
Article Summary: A physical education teacher has been suspended following a protocol lapse during the opening ceremony of the state-level 67th Republic Day Athletics Competitions. The incident occurred when the state transport minister A Vijay Tamilan Parthiban was hoisting the national flag. A snag in the rope caused the flag to fly upside down.

Article Title: Two history-sheeters who escaped from Attayampatti police station nabbed
Article Text: SALEM: Two history-sheeters, who escaped from the Attayampatti police station in Salem district on Tuesday, were nabbed in the early hours of Wednesday.The duo, identified as Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu, are residents of Kandarkula Manickam near Attayampatti. According to police, Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu were brought to the Attayampatti police station on Tuesday morning in connection with robbery and theft cases and questioned by sub-inspector Krishnan and other police personnel. Subsequently, cases were registered against them.Later, police were making arrangements to produce them before a court in the evening. “However, taking advantage of an opportunity, Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu managed to escape from the police station,” said a police officer.Special police teams were formed to trace them. After an intensive search operation, the duo were tracked down and arrested from near Tiruchengode around 3am on Wednesday.They were brought back to the Attayampatti police station for further inquiry. Later, they were lodged in the Salem Central Prison under judicial custody.
Article Summary: The duo, identified as Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu, are residents of Kandarkula Manickam near Attayampatti. They were brought to the police station on Tuesday morning in connection with robbery and theft cases and questioned by sub- inspector Krishnan and other police personnel.

Article Title: Nedumbassery car crash: Kerala HC to consider 4th accused’s bail plea on Friday
Article Text:
Kochi:





The high court on Tuesday sought instructions from the state govt on a bail petition filed by Ameen Shah, the fourth accused in the Nedumbassery car crash case. A bench of Justice Kauser Edappagath adjourned the petition to Nov 6 to consider it along with the bail petitions of two other accused, Suhail Sajeev and Joel S Anto.According to the prosecution, Suhail (19) allegedly drove a Mini Cooper at a speed exceeding 100kmphon the airport road at Nedumbassery in the early hours of Oct 11 while heavily intoxicated. The car rammed into a scooter carrying three youngsters — Iyas, Devika and Gopika — resulting in their deaths. His friends Ninav, Ameen and Joel, who were also in the car, have been arrayed as co-accused in the case.On Oct 17, the Angamaly judicial first-class magistrate court dismissed the bail pleas of all four accused. The additional district and sessions court, Ernakulam, also rejected their pleas on Oct 28. The accused subsequently approached the HC.
Article Summary: The high court sought instructions from the state govt on a bail petition filed by Ameen Shah, the fourth accused in the Nedumbassery car crash case. The court adjourned the petition to Nov 6 to consider it along with the bail petitions of two other accused, Suhail Sajeev and Joel S Anto.
